And so now I'll turn it over to Dr. Hinton. Thank you, Madam Chair, members of the board, and Dr. Cashwell. In 2017-18, Henrico County Public Schools undertook a comprehensive effort to craft a strategic plan for 2018 through 2025, which is known as Destination 2025.

The creation of the plan included diverse stakeholders and a variety of feedback mechanisms. Throughout that year, the HCPS community participated in focus groups, community input events, work groups, online public comments, surveys, and a public hearing to share their input on what the school division was doing well and how we could improve.

A key component of the creation of Destination 2025 was the Strategic Plan Steering Committee, which included representation from students, families, staff, and community members across all magisterial districts, as well as two school board representatives.

This committee examined school division data and used community feedback to create the plan's strategic goals, action steps, and progress metrics. Since adoption of the plan in 2018, the Steering Committee has met annually to review the plan and ensure progress towards our goals.

Any proposed revisions have been taken to the school board for consideration and approval. I would like to take a moment to express our gratitude to Ms. Kinsella and Ms. Shea for your ongoing commitment and service to the Strategic Plan Steering Committee. Your dedication and insights have been instrumental in shaping the progress of our school division over the past six years.

Also, a warm welcome to Mr. Irving, our new school board representative on this committee. We are looking forward to our collaboration with you and Ms. Shea in our planning efforts as we move forward in this process. Our current plan will guide us through the spring of 2025.

However, we want to share an overview of the process for the creation of a new strategic plan, which will be adopted by the 2025-26 school year. The plan development process will continue to be a collaborative effort between all stakeholders within the HCPS community and will build upon the successes of Destination 2025.

Throughout the remainder of the school year, a range of activities is underway to set the foundation for the development of the 2025-2030 plan. This fall, division leadership began the process of defining key planning components and throughout the winter will work on drafting HCPS's vision, mission, and core values.

In January, staff will begin conducting focus groups with each school board and superintendent advisory committee, along with other essential community partners, to gather valuable insights into HCPS's strengths and areas for improvement.

To capture additional community perspectives, annual stakeholder surveys will be conducted in February. This feedback will be instrumental in the fall and winter of 2024 when the new Strategic Plan Steering Committee will be tasked with refining the strategic plan components and identifying strategic goals.

The draft plan will be shared with the HCPS community in the spring of 2025 and feedback will be used to further refine the plan before seeking school board approval. The new 2025-2030 strategic plan will be launched beginning in the summer of 2025.

As we gather insights in the coming months, our attention will center on three key areas. First, we'll explore foundational principles, diving into how HCPS's vision, mission, and core values align with community expectations and needs.
